Let the storefront do the storefront: Discovery, search and a published catalog are real work, and none of it happens here. The accounts who want to browse keep browsing. The ones who just want Friday's order reordered get a quicker route to it.
Money and paperwork stay put: Our app never touches money. Nothing about adding it asks you to move how customers pay or how invoices go out, which is usually the part nobody wants to disturb.

@graph.name: Three steps, and no launch date
@graph.description: Nothing here needs a project plan, and Cut+Dry carries on as normal. You send guides, we set up accounts, your kitchens start ordering.

step.name: Hand us your guides
step.text: Whatever format they are already in. Each account's lines and your prices go into a single admin screen, lined up with your codes.

step.name: We set up each account
step.text: We open an account for each kitchen, and the kitchen installs our app. Most have ordered before the day is out.

step.name: It turns up priced
step.text: Signed off by the buyer, carrying a number and a time, in the shape your system expects.

@graph.name: Does adding voice orders mean finding a Cut+Dry alternative?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Cut+Dry's call transcription already turns what callers say into orders, and it carries on unchanged. What VoiceOrder Solutions adds beside it is an app where the account talks through its order and approves the lines itself. The ones who browse your storefront keep browsing, and nothing gets switched off first.

@graph.name: Is VoiceOrder Solutions better than Cut+Dry?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not at selling a catalog, collecting money, or the manufacturer side of their network. Those are what they built, and we would not ask you to give them up. Where we help is the reorder from an account you already have, spoken off your guide and approved before it sends. That narrow job is often what a Cut+Dry alternative search was really about.

@graph.name: Does VoiceOrder Solutions link up with Cut+Dry?

acceptedAnswer.text: It does not. The two products have no connection, and neither vendor supports the other. Each passes its orders to your own system on its own, ours in the formats listed above. When ours come in by EDI or the API, both end up in the same system; an emailed order arrives as a file to open like any other email.

@graph.name: Will some kitchens be using two ordering apps?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only the ones you offer it to. Accounts happy ordering through Cut+Dry can stay there. The app is for kitchens that still pick up the phone, which is where a spoken, checked order frees up your desk the most. Calls you keep taking get no order number from us; only what is sent through our app does.

@graph.name: What if a cook gets pulled away halfway through an order?

acceptedAnswer.text: Their list stays saved where they stopped, so they can pick it up again when they are back, and nothing goes out until they send it.

@graph.name: How quickly can accounts start sending orders?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most distributors this is live inside 24 to 48 hours, with a first order usually in on the same day. Nothing about your Cut+Dry setup has to change while it goes in.
Neither of us publishes a figure. Cut+Dry has a pricing page with no prices on it, and ours comes as a quote. Since that platform is staying, the thing to price is only what the voice reorder adds.

@graph.name: Where do the Cut+Dry details on this page come from?

acceptedAnswer.text: All of the above was read on their own site, 10 October 2026: the module descriptions, the line about transcribing calls and the published 90 day launch. We have left their growth percentages alone, because those are their numbers. If any of it has moved on, the fault is here, not there.
